summary: The milestone-scoped timing detector reported 0 experiments / 0 wall-time minutes / 0 compute-bound tasks for 2026.06.395, so the locked numeric fields stay at zero per the anti-hallucination guard. This is the SAME recurring false-zero detector artifact documented across .363-.394, not an empty milestone: on-disk results/ artifacts for this window indicate experiments did run; the detector simply failed to attribute their commits to the milestone. No wall-time bottleneck can be measured from a zero-row timing feed.
bottlenecks_identified: Recurring milestone-scoped timing-detector false-zero: the authoritative timing feed reported 0 experiment commits even though on-disk results/ artifacts exist for this window. This is an OBSERVABILITY bug (commit-to-milestone attribution), not an execution or wall-time bottleneck, and it has now recurred across .363-.395.

Because no compute-bound task appears in the timing data, the observed 0% GPU utilization on both RTX 3090s is expected idle state at the snapshot, NOT a bottleneck (per the GPU-idle interpretation rule, GPU idle is only a bug when a compute-bound task is present; gpu_idle_on_compute_bound_tasks is therefore null).
improvements_suggested: Fix the milestone-scoped timing detector so it attributes experiment commits to the active milestone (the recurring root cause of the false-zero across .363-.395). Candidate: key off the activation commit boundary and the on-disk results/experiment_*.json mtimes rather than whatever window heuristic currently misses them.

Until the detector is repaired, have the retro fall back to on-disk results/ mtimes plus the ops/changelog.md milestone window so the wall-time and slowest-experiment analysis can still be produced instead of degrading to a zero-row report.
Emit a detector_gap_suspected flag whenever the timing feed reports 0 experiments but on-disk artifacts exist for the window, so a false-zero is never silently read as a clean or empty milestone.
top_3_highest_leverage_actions: Repair the milestone-scoped timing detector (commit-to-milestone attribution) so retros stop degrading to false-zero; this is the single highest-leverage operational fix and has been outstanding for 30+ milestones.
Wire an on-disk results/ mtime fallback into the retro path so a detector miss does not erase the entire timing analysis.
Auto-raise detector_gap_suspected when timing reports 0 but on-disk artifacts exist, making the false-zero self-evident rather than ambiguous.
meta_reflection: Reflecting on HOW rather than WHAT: execution this milestone was fine; the operational failure is observability. The retro's own input feed reported zero experiments while artifacts sat on disk, the same false-zero seen since .363. The highest-value process fix is not a faster experiment but a timing detector that actually finds the work, plus a detector_gap_suspected tripwire so the gap can never again masquerade as an empty milestone.
